title: Windows Hopper keyboard shortcut does not work in Rider.

judgment.rationale: The issue clearly says Window Hopper fails only in Rider, but current code filters to Alt-Tab-eligible top-level windows for the foreground process, so a small amount of Rider-specific window/elevation evidence is still needed.
evidence: The reporter says the hotkey works in other apps and fails only in Rider.
AltWindowCycle.cpp only includes windows that are visible, not cloaked, and are the Alt-Tab representative for their ownership chain.
No recording, Rider version, or elevation details are attached.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for a short Rider-specific recording and configuration details that map directly to Window Hopper eligibility logic.

fix_assessment.rationale: There is not yet enough Rider-specific evidence to choose between eligibility filtering, elevation isolation, and shortcut interception.

issue_context.summary: Window Hopper fails only for Rider windows, and the current implementation selects Alt-Tab-eligible top-level windows from the foreground process, so the remaining gap is what kind of Rider windows are present when the shortcut is pressed.
known_information: The user has multiple Rider windows and the hotkey works in other apps.
The report does not include Rider version, window layout, elevation state, or a recording.
Window Hopper groups candidates by the real foreground process image path.
inferences: Rider may be exposing owned/tool windows that fail the Alt-Tab eligibility check, or it may be intercepting the hotkey first.
A short recording and exact Rider configuration would materially narrow those possibilities.
issue_context.analysis: A generic bugreport request would be wasteful. The actionable gap is precise Rider window behavior compared with AltWindowCycle eligibility rules.

information_gaps.information: A short recording showing multiple Rider windows, the Window Hopper shortcut press, and the absence of thumbnails.
information_gaps.why_needed: It confirms whether the overlay never appears or appears without candidates.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Please capture a short screen recording focused on the shortcut press with at least two Rider windows visible and upload it through the GitHub web UI.

information_gaps.information: The exact Rider version/build, whether Rider is running elevated, and whether any Rider keymap is bound to the same shortcut.
information_gaps.why_needed: That distinguishes candidate filtering from app-level hotkey interception or elevation isolation.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Please reply with the Rider version/build, whether Rider runs elevated, and whether the same key combination is assigned inside Rider or another JetBrains tool.

information_gaps.information: Whether the two Rider items are separate top-level windows or only tabs/panels inside one Rider window.
information_gaps.why_needed: Window Hopper cycles windows, not internal tabs, so this changes the expected candidate set.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Please confirm whether the affected Rider items are separate Windows taskbar windows or only tabs/panels inside one Rider window.

comment.body:
Thanks for narrowing this to Rider only. Window Hopper currently cycles Alt-Tab-eligible top-level windows from the foreground process, so the next useful evidence is very specific:

1. Please upload a short recording showing at least two Rider windows, the Window Hopper shortcut press, and the fact that no thumbnails appear.
2. Please reply with the exact Rider version/build, whether Rider is running elevated, and whether Rider or another JetBrains tool is bound to the same shortcut.
3. Please confirm whether the affected Rider items are separate taskbar windows or only tabs/panels inside one Rider window.

Those details will tell us whether Rider windows are being filtered out or the hotkey is intercepted before Window Hopper can cycle them.

design_decision.reason: Rider-specific window evidence is still missing.

confidence.rationale: Owning eligibility code is narrow, but Rider window shape is still unknown.
